arguments.conclusion: The 50-year mortgage will drive up home prices and worsen long-term affordability.

arguments.premise_synthesis: The 50-year mortgage proposal increases affordability by only a couple hundred dollars per month. The average American lives paycheck to paycheck and would use the extra borrowing to buy a more expensive home, not to invest. This artificially increased demand drives up prices, mirroring the effect of the 30-year mortgage which similarly drove up prices.
arguments.conclusion_supported: It establishes that the 50-year mortgage, as a government intervention, will lead to higher home prices and worsen long-term affordability.

source_speech_filenames: 20260112_The Government is Taking Over the US Housing Market.txt
relationship_explanations: The speech argues that excessive government intervention is the root cause of the housing crisis and critiques specific policy proposals (50-year mortgage, ban on institutional investors, government MBS purchases) as ineffective band-aids that worsen the problem, directly supporting the canonical claim that government intervention causes housing unaffordability and other economic problems.
